title: Nobody Knows
sketch: A: narrative ballad. The idea travels through a mind, ink, numbers, a screen, and finally a song; slow waltz in dorian.
refrain: Who made this song? No-bo-dy knows.
It came through the win-dow and out it goes.
It's yours while you sing it, and then it's gone,
so learn it by heart, and then pass it on.

lines: [someone] put it into [a vehicle] [when or where]
[how far or how long it went]

hooks.why: 'out it goes' rhymes with 'song' on the high tonic

seed_verses: There once was a thought in a qui-et man's head;
he kept it so close that it nev-er was said.
It walked where he walked, and it slept where he slept;
they bur-ied it with him, the se-cret he kept.
A girl wrote it down by a can-dle one night,
in ink on a page, and she fold-ed it tight.
It sailed the gray wa-ter and slept in a drawer,
and no-bo-dy speaks like she wrote a-ny-more.
They saved it as num-bers, a flick-er of light,
and cop-ied it round the whole world in a night.
Each cop-y was per-fect{perfect} in ev-ery last part,
but not one ma-chine ev-er knew it by heart.
The whole world was watch-ing it all in a day,
a mil-lion bright fac-es all lit the same way.
They laughed and they wept, and they scrolled on and on,
and no-bo-dy sang it, and then it was gone.
A sail-or was hum-ming it down by the quay;
a girl sell-ing or-an-ges caught it for free.
She had-n't his lan-guage, she had-n't his name;
she gave it her own words and sang it the same.
